s1_title: All three NGM clusters are saving money with CAST AI
s1_subtitle: Realized savings · September 2026 · CAST AI Savings Report (EU API, discounted basis — re-verified 2026-10-05)
s1_footnote: * Gross = CAST AI realized savings: what the clusters would have cost at the frozen pre-onboarding baseline minus what they actually cost — a counterfactual, not an invoice line. Net = gross − platform fee (€5 × avg provisioned vCPU·month ≈ €8.9k helios, €5.0k integ, €0.4k kronos). API re-pull 2026-10-05 matches every cell within $1.15. Kronos baseline is ~12 months old (cpuOP 5.25×, memOP 11×) — treat its $3.5k as directional pending re-baseline.
s1_why_title: Why doesn't the customer see it on their bill?
s1_why_bullets: It's a counterfactual, not an invoice line.
Savings appear only as a lower unit price: $/vCPU-day fell Jul→Sep on every cluster (helios −7.9%, integ $0.813 → $0.731, kronos ER 0.62).
Demand growth eats the unit-price win.
integ +14.8% and kronos +42% provisioned vCPU Aug→Sep — bills rise or stay flat while the price per vCPU drops.
The €5/vCPU platform fee sits between gross and net.
≈ $16.4k/month across the three clusters — visible on their invoice, deducted from the savings view.
Different ruler + storage outside the math.
They read Cloudability/SAP in EUR (paid, RI/SP-discounted); the API is USD compute-only. Storage = 7–16% of each bill and never appears in savings.
s1_notes: Evidence (all read-only GETs against api.eu.cast.ai, 2026-10-05). Period = September 2026 calendar month; GET /v1/cost-reports/clusters/{id}/savings, DAILY step required (hourly step undercounts ~7×). summary.totalSavings: helios $18,877.78 vs deck $18,878.73 (Δ$0.95); integ $18,512.46 vs $18,513.61 (Δ$1.15, recompute drift since PPT generation); kronos $3,501.32 vs $3,501.35 (Δ$0.03). Trailing-30d does NOT match — the deck period is the calendar month. Net verified: fee = €5 × summary.avgCpuCount (helios 1,786.3, integ 1,005.9, kronos 86.58 vCPU) at EUR/USD ≈ 1.14 → nets $8,695.90 / $12,780.11 / $3,007.82 vs deck $8,696.34 / $12,780.10 / $3,007.78. Why invisible: (1) counterfactual baseline model — projected = frozen pre-CAST-AI baseline × demand; (2) unit price fell but demand grew (integ +14.8% vCPU, OD compute +$2,374 MoM; kronos +42%); (3) fee basis avgCpuCount (this is also Gerolf's billable-CPU invoice math); (4) storage outside savings: helios $8,812 (16.3% of $53,908 bill), integ $1,786 (7.5%), kronos $327 (14.4%); (5) customer ruler = Cloudability/SAP EUR amortized RI/SP — compare deltas and ER, never levels, until d is pinned from their Cloudability export. Spot spend = $0 on all three (spotInstances.enabled=false). Workload autoscaler: 0 workloads optimized on all three (helios 3,628 policy-assigned but appliedPods=0; integ 1,523 recommend-only; kronos 263 READ_ONLY) → WAS savings $0; all realized savings come from node downscaling/bin-packing.

s2_notes: Verification (read-only, 2026-10-05): helios estimated-savings (LISTING basis) rightsizing $35,208 / spot $39,335 / spot-only $61,964 — deck ≈ 0.5× listing, i.e. discounted-scaled; integ live snapshot discounted rightsizing $4,212 / spot $4,283 / ARM $5,845, but estimated-savings-history shows deck values matched Oct-3 low-demand hours ($2,593 @06:00Z, $2,614 @00:00Z); kronos deck values match a single 2026-08-26T17:00Z peak hour (~180 vCPU) — September monthly averages are $385 (rightsizing) / $489 (spot), so the deck overstates kronos ~6–7× and the 10→3-node story is a peak-hour projection (fleet already = 3 nodes off-peak; weekday peaks 34–104 nodes). ARM is an external model everywhere. Kronos rebalancing: 30/50 recent scheduled plans status=error, 0 ops, isRebalancingRecommended=true — fix before committing dates.
